problem.summary: 大规模人脸识别中，深度卷积神经网络（DCNNs）的特征学习面临设计合适损失函数以增强判别力的挑战。

motivation.summary: 现有方法如Centre Loss在欧氏空间中惩罚特征与类中心的距离，SphereFace在角度空间中以乘法方式惩罚角度。研究趋势是在损失函数中引入间隔以最大化人脸类间可分性。

core_idea.summary: 提出加性角度间隔损失（ArcFace），通过在角度空间中添加加性间隔，获得高度判别性的人脸特征。该方法具有清晰的几何解释，与超球面上的测地距离精确对应。

method.summary: 基于ArcFace损失函数，通过在最后一层全连接层的权重与特征向量之间的角度上添加一个固定的加性间隔，来增强类内紧凑性和类间可分性。

experiments.summary: 在十个人脸识别基准上进行了广泛的实验评估，包括一个新的具有万亿对的大规模图像数据库和一个大规模视频数据集。

metadata.title: ArcFace: Additive Angular Margin Loss for Deep Face Recognition

metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / CNN / Top-cited ML method paper
metadata.abstract: One of the main challenges in feature learning using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks (DCNNs) for large-scale face recognition is the design of appropriate loss functions that can enhance the discriminative power. Centre loss penalises the distance between deep features and their corresponding class centres in the Euclidean space to achieve intra-class compactness. SphereFace assumes that the linear transformation matrix in the last fully connected layer can be used as a representation of the class centres in the angular space and therefore penalises the angles between deep features and their corresponding weights in a multiplicative way. Recently, a popular line of research is to incorporate margins in well-established loss functions in order to maximise face class separability. In this paper, we propose an Additive Angular Margin Loss (ArcFace) to obtain highly discriminative features for face recognition. The proposed ArcFace has a clear geometric interpretation due to its exact correspondence to geodesic distance on a hypersphere. We present arguably the most extensive experimental evaluation against all recent state-of-the-art face recognition methods on ten face recognition benchmarks which includes a new large-scale image database with trillions of pairs and a large-scale video dataset. We show that ArcFace consistently outperforms the state of the art and can be easily implemented with negligible computational overhead. To facilitate future research, the code has been made available.
